newsitem.title: UK: Russia's leading retailer sees expansion, profits.
newsitem.headline: Russia's leading retailer sees expansion, profits.

text.p: Russia's leading department store, Trade House GUM, told investors in London Thursday it aimed to boost profits and double space at its prestigious Red Square building in Moscow.

Company Vice President Anatoly Stepanov said on Thursday that GUM would spend $192 million on refurbishing its main department store and build new stores outside Moscow. Stepanov also said he saw a rapid rise in profitability.
"We are consistently increasing sales and improving service. Our aim is to more than double retail space in our building in Red Square," he said.

GUM's main Moscow store, which occupies a prime spot opposite the Kremlin, has been transformed from dictator Josef Stalin's "Showcase of Socialism and its achievements" into a seller of chic Western consumer goods with brand names like Christian Dior and Levi.
It boasts that sales per square meter are on a par with stores on New York's Fifth Avenue.
Targeting Russia's new rich has paid off and sales have risen from $103 million in 1992 to $199 million in 1995 and are seen growing to $250 million this year.
Profits have also risen, and GUM expects net income to rise to $50 million in 1995 from last year's $29.5 million.
